Calibrate an intensity intervention to a target value

Source: R/calibrate-alpha.R
calibrate_alpha.Rd

Finds the intervention alpha on the intensity of the process z_name such that the estimated risk of z_name equals a calibration target, and estimates the risk of target under that calibrated intervention. The standard error of the latter accounts for the estimation of alpha.

Usage

calibrate_alpha(
  initial_fit,
  target,
  z_name = "z",
  theta = NULL,
  rho = NULL,
  delta = NULL,
  rho_1a = NULL,
  a = NULL,
  cores = 1,
  verbose = FALSE,
  ...
)

Arguments

initial_fit

An initial fit, as returned by fit_initial().

target

Character vector. Names of the processes whose risks are estimated under the calibrated intervention.

z_name

String. Name of the process whose intensity alpha scales. If no such process exists in initial_fit, alpha is ignored with a warning.

theta, rho, delta, rho_1a

Numbers specifying the calibration target, see Description. Give exactly one.

a

Optional baseline treatment value (0 or 1) to intervene on. Must be one of the values of a given to fit_initial().

cores

Positive integer. Number of cores used by parallel::mclapply() for the per-individual computations.

verbose

Logical. If TRUE, print progress.

...

Further arguments passed on to tmle_alpha().

Value

A list with elements:

  • estimate: a named vector with the calibrated alpha_est and its alpha_se, the risk of target (target_est) with standard error target_se (accounting for the estimation of alpha) and target_se_crude (treating alpha as known), and the calibration target theta with standard error theta_se.

  • checks: diagnostics of the alpha search and derivative estimates.

  • alpha_eic, target_eic and eic: the influence curves of the calibrated alpha, of the risk of target treating alpha as known, and of the risk of target.

With several targets, the per-target entries of estimate and checks are suffixed by the target name (e.g. target_est_death), and target_eic and eic are lists named by target.

Details

Exactly one of theta, rho, delta and rho_1a specifies the calibration target:

  • theta: the risk of z_name itself.

  • rho: a fraction of the risk of z_name without intervention.

  • delta: an absolute difference from the risk of z_name without intervention.

  • rho_1a: a fraction of the risk of z_name without intervention on z_name, under the opposite baseline treatment 1 - a.

Examples

fit <- fit_initial(
  illness_death,
  fit_types = list(
    z = list(
      delta = 2,
      model = ~ L0,
      at_risk = function(dt) dt[["z"]] == 0
    ),
    death = list(delta = 1, model = ~ L0 + z),
    censoring = list(delta = 0, model = ~ L0)
  ),
  tau = 1
)

# Risk of death under the intervention on z that brings the risk of z
# down to 80% of its observed value.
cal <- calibrate_alpha(fit, target = "death", z_name = "z", rho = 0.8)
cal$estimate
#>       alpha_est        alpha_se      target_est       target_se target_se_crude 
#>      0.79272380      0.00995552      0.31992034      0.03864198      0.03866085 
#>           theta        theta_se 
#>      0.12713026      0.02505712
